{"notes": "VISIT 3 (7:45). Table: the line is dark and connected from START along the top, round the nose, and along the bottom to the lower tail tip at about (28,15.5). The same stray pair is still pale near (6.2-6.7,12.9). The doubled parallel stretch on the lower left (x 5-11, y 13-14.7) is still there, connected but redundant. Nothing was cleaned up, and the whole table is now hands off. The strays are off the path, so the risk is low. The overlap is connected, but a double run could topple oddly at the review. Check how the fall behaves there.

LEO: Report matches the picture: connected nearly end to end, two strays. He said he checked the nose closely. He is accurate and calm, and he called the hands-off decision. He still hasn't mentioned the double run. Solid execution and collaboration.

MAYA: Private summary is accurate: about 117 of 119 connected, which fits the two strays. She credits others correctly and did the tail fork and the end-to-end check, as she said she would. Strong ownership. Her 'nothing needs fixing' is slightly complacent, since she skips the overlap and strays. Leadership is quiet but real.

TOM: His nose join is visible and connected, and his report is honest and matches Leo's and Maya's. Following up and finishing the check shows reliability. He is still lower-profile than Maya and Leo, but no longer passive.

PRIYA: Said nothing this visit, and I have no new evidence. Her top line is clean and strong, and her earlier delegation and fall check were good. She may have driven the hands-off decision, but I can't confirm it. Ask her at the review what she did in the final stretch.

NEXT: Watch the fall. See whether the strays and the double run matter, and whose idea hands-off was."}
